related_questions.question: Do subsequent COVID infections get worse?
related_questions.snippet: Getting COVID a second time can lead to worsened long COVID symptoms, and possibly long-term impacts on your heart, lungs and brain.
related_questions.title: Repeat COVID Infections: A Danger to Your Health? - Jefferson Health

related_questions.question: How is COVID-19 an example of viral evolution?
related_questions.snippet: Some viruses change quickly and others more slowly. SARS-CoV-2, the virus which causes COVID-19, tends to change more slowly than others such as HIV or influenza viruses. This could in part be explained by the virus's internal “proofreading mechanism” which can correct “mistakes” when it makes copies of itself.

related_questions.question: How long will COVID remain infectious?
related_questions.snippet: While people become less contagious over time, they are still contagious with COVID for an average of eight days. That may vary depending on factors including underlying health conditions and the severity of illness.
related_questions.title: How Long Am I Contagious? - Yale New Haven Hospital

related_questions.question: How many times can a person be infected with COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People can be reinfected with SARS-CoV-2 multiple times. Each time a person is infected with SARS-CoV-2, they have a risk of developing Long COVID. Long COVID symptoms and conditions can emerge, persist, resolve, and reemerge over weeks and months.
